judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate claims-made caption in capitals; nothing in it names a term with two reasonable meanings, though 'reported ... during the policy period' is stated absolutely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states claims must be reported during the policy period, while Insuring Agreements I.A/I.B and Section VIII permit reporting in an 'extended reporting period', a mild tension a court could be asked to harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short integration statement listing the documents that make up the policy; its wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives no order of precedence among Declarations, policy form and the sixteen endorsements, several of which (Endorsements 5, 8, 10, 11) purport to delete and replace the same provisions, so a priority question could arise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '100 % minimum-earned' is a definite figure, but the sentence is garbled ('Item. 2.a and/or litem, 3.a.') and 'whichever is earlier' adds a small mechanical wrinkle.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Condition IX.A.3 contemplates 'remaining unearned premium, if any' being refunded pro rata on cancellation, which is hard to reconcile with a 100% minimum-earned premium.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical capitalised notice in the policy form; standard and definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same tension as the Declarations notice with the 'extended reporting period' allowance in I.A, I.B and Section VIII.B.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple statement that quoted words are defined in Section V; nothing ambiguous in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6 uses the quoted term 'covered operations', which appears nowhere in Section V or any endorsement, so the promise that all quoted words are defined is not fully kept.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary consideration and reliance recital; no term with competing meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with IX.F Representations and the Fraud exclusion; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in conditioning coverage on the Declarations identifying the coverage; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Items 2 and 3 of the Declarations, both of which are completed; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Arising out of a pollution condition on, at, under, or migrating from a covered location' and 'first commence, in their entirety, during the policy period' are the classic battlegrounds of a pollution policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This subsection is deleted and replaced twice over — by Endorsement 5.II and again by Endorsement 10.I — with different substitute texts, leaving a genuine question which version governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'First commenced, in whole or part, prior to the policy period' is workable but sits against Coverage A's 'in their entirety', and 'nolicy period' is a typo.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Coverage A and the Known Conditions exclusion, the A/B boundary for a condition straddling inception is not obviously resolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and one-directional but definite: the retention must be paid before the Insurer's obligation attaches.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with V.AA, III.A and IX.D Bankruptcy, which expressly preserves the retention obligation; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A per-condition limit tied to Item 2.b; the only soft edge is 'same, continuous, repeated, or related'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.I deletes and replaces this subsection with a version omitting 'legal defense expense', so the superseded original could be invoked against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Calls Item 2.c 'the maximum liability of the Insurer pursuant to this Policy', which is an overstatement given Item 4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 2.c is $9,000,000 while the Item 4 Total Policy Aggregate in II.G is $7,000,000, an arithmetic incoherence in the Declarations; the subsection is also replaced by Endorsement 6.I.D.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirror of the Coverage A per-condition limit; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Replaced by Endorsement 6.I.E, whose substitute adds the undefined qualifier 'resulting from covered operations'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard aggregate wording, again describing Item 3.c as 'the maximum liability ... pursuant to this Policy'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coverage B aggregate ($5m) plus Coverage A aggregate ($9m) exceed the $7m Total Policy Aggregate, and Endorsement 6.I.F replaces this text with a 'covered operations' version.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to Subsections C., D., E. and F.' is an odd cross-reference for a cap that is meant to override them, but the sentence itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $7,000,000 Item 4 aggregate is smaller than the $9,000,000 Coverage A aggregate in Item 2.c, so the per-coverage limits and the total cap cannot both be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deeming language is long but definite; 'continuous, repeated, or related' carries some vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'No other policy shall respond' bears on the prior-year policy PPL G24551532 001 identified on the Declarations as the renewed policy, a live relationship question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Duty-to-defend wording is conventional and its termination triggers are enumerated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.II deletes and replaces this subsection with a version adding exhaustion of the defence sublimit; the superseded text remains printed in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable proximity', 'similar complexity' and 'suitable' errors-and-omissions cover are soft, but each is a customary rate-and-qualification standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits comfortably with III.A, III.E and IX.M Consent; no direct conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Right and the duty to retain' a consultant subject to the Insurer's prior written consent is clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4.III deletes this subsection entirely and substitutes a consultant/catastrophe-management-firm version, so the printed text is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, definite: defence costs erode limits and apply to the retention.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.II.D replaces it with a version applying defence costs to a dedicated $2m sublimit and Item 4, so the two erosion schemes must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Does not impose any additional unreasonable burdens on the insured' is a soft standard inside an otherwise mechanical consent-to-settle clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.IV.F restates a similar hammer clause in garbled form, creating two overlapping versions of the same mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Located, and claims made, within the United States of America' is a bright line; only 'located' for a migrating condition is faintly soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the scheduled locations in Endorsements 5 and 11, all of which are domestic; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Self-referential but definite: additional insureds have only the rights the endorsement gives them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Endorsement 2, which limits Hoffman Rettig to vicarious liability; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but enumerated definition; 'prospective medical monitoring costs' is limited by its own purpose clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in the Employers Liability exclusion and definitions of 'claim'; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires mutual agreement and describes qualifications; definite though dependent on cooperation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The role exists only to price fungi/legionella remediation, which Endorsement 12 excludes outright, leaving the definition with nothing to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Written assertion of a legal right ... including, but not limited to, a government action' is a general-plus-specific formulation whose reach is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This definition is deleted and replaced twice, by Endorsement 8.II.D and Endorsement 11.II.D, each 'solely with respect to' its own coverage, leaving the operative baseline uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed description of third-party carriage with a clear end-point at unloading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10 deletes Subsection E and substitutes 'Transportation', so the term 'contingent transportation' still used in base exclusion Q has no surviving definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-limb list keyed to schedules; the numbering is corrupted (the first item lost its '1.') but the sense is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both Endorsement 8.I and Endorsement 11.I purport to delete Subsection F 'in its entirety' and replace it with different lists, a direct competition between two replacements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Imminent and substantial threat' is a standard regulatory phrase and the 72-hour window is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with III.C, VII.C and the Internal Expenses exclusion carve-out; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditioned on an explicit contract listed on a schedule; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Schedule of Insured Contracts Endorsement is attached, so the Contractual Liability exception in VI.B has nothing to bite on — an illusory carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sweeping list ending in 'guidance document' and 'risk-based corrective action guidance'; whether non-binding guidance counts is genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It controls 'remediation costs' and 'government action', so its breadth drives whether agency depopulation-type directives trigger coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'First made against the insured during or subsequent to the end of the policy period' is oddly worded for a reporting-period definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VIII.B deems such claims made on the last day of the policy period, and Endorsement 7 changes the durations, so the definition must be read with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assigns agency and payment responsibility precisely; no competing readings apparent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with V.S, VIII and IX.A; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Circular ('byproducts produced or released by fungi') but the class is understood.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 both removes fungi from 'pollution condition' and adds a fungi exclusion, leaving this definition largely inoperative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Action taken or liability imposed ... acting pursuant to the authority of environmental law' turns on the borrowed breadth of 'environmental law'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds directly into the definition of 'claim' and hence into whether regulatory directives are covered; the dependency is real but internally consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long enumerated list with an 'including' catch-all, but the three qualifying conditions are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Carried forward unchanged into the Endorsement 12 definition of 'pollution condition'; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition uses the defined word inside itself ('employee of ... any insured'), a circularity that leaves its outer edge fuzzy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with the Insured vs. Insured exclusion and the Separation of Insureds condition, which speak of 'named insured' rather than 'insured' — an imperfect fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable legal costs, charges, and expenses, including expert charges' is customary; 'reasonable' is the only soft word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6 removes defence expense from the per-condition limits while adding a dedicated sublimit, but the definition itself is untouched.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by exclusion of listed categories with 'specified quantities' left unspecified, a small vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only within 'pollution condition'; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Anchored to two named federal statutes; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only within 'pollution condition' and 'illicit abandonment'; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear equivalence of rights subject to a stated carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with V.K and the Separation of Insureds condition; Endorsement 1 supplies the single named insured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An exhaustive statutory-style definition; long but internally precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 sublimits natural resource damage claims to $500,000, which is consistent rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very short and broad — 'any disposal site or recycling facility ... which receives, or has historically received' an insured's waste.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8.II replaces Subsection U with a much narrower, condition-laden definition, so the printed baseline is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb 2 is syntactically mangled ('the period of time following the closing date ... or, as applicable, through the applicable expiration date'), obscuring when that period starts and ends.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Automatic Acquisition Endorsement is attached, so limb 2 is inoperative, but the term drives every reporting condition in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant, contaminant, or pollutant, including ...' is the archetypal general-versus-specific pollution list that courts repeatedly construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 deletes this subsection in its entirety and substitutes a version dropping fungi and excluding odour, so the printed text is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated limbs, each conventional; 'diminished value' is defined by reference to third-party ownership.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits against the First-Party Property Damage exclusion, which is a deliberate complement rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent required by environmental law' and 'reasonable expenses' are the standard fighting words of remediation-cost coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its fungi/legionella fallback depends on a 'certified industrial hygienist', yet Endorsement 12 excludes fungi and legionella entirely, leaving that sentence stranded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any employee ... responsible for environmental affairs, control, or compliance' is a knowledge-attribution test whose boundary is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gates the Known Conditions, Intentional Non-Compliance, Fraud and UST exclusions, so its breadth propagates, but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure pointer to Declarations Items 2.d and 3.d; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4 adds a separate catastrophe-specific retention of the same amount without saying whether both can apply to one event.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Commission or threat of a dangerous act' and intent-based limbs are notoriously elastic, though this is standard TRIA-style wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the War or Terrorism exclusion; consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A quantified test (more than ten percent below ground) with two express carve-outs; unusually precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in exclusion VI.P, which refers to schedules that are not attached, but the definition itself fits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long disjunctive list ending in 'damage of property by any government, military or other authority', which is far wider than war and could swallow ordinary regulatory action.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the War or Terrorism exclusion, that final limb could exclude government-ordered destruction of property, an uncomfortable fit with 'government action' coverage in the definition of 'claim'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Arising out of or related to' asbestos with a soil-and-groundwater carve-back; broad but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the parallel lead-paint exclusion; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'except if the liability would have attached in the absence of such contract' proviso is standard but litigation-prone in application.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its carve-out for 'environmental indemnity obligations' depends on a Schedule of Insured Contracts Endorsement that is not attached, so the exception is empty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sold, abandoned, or given away ... or was condemned' is enumerated and the timing test is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'This exclusion shall not apply to Coverage B' is coherent with I.B, which covers only pre-existing conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional employers-liability wording; the sub-list numbering is corrupted ('4.' for '1.') but meaning is unaffected.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps the Insured vs. Insured exclusion given that 'insured' includes employees, but the two are complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any associated claims seeking exclusively injunctive relief in addition to such fines' is close to unintelligible, and the punitive-damages carve-back reverses part of the first sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-back turns on damages being 'insurable by law', which under the New York choice-of-law clause materially changes the result — a real cross-provision dependency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear first-party bar with an express carve-back for remediation costs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the definition of 'property damage' (third-party property) and with 'remediation costs'; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Materiality tied to what would have affected the underwriting decision; conventional and reasonably precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interlocks with IX.A.2.b cancellation and IX.F Representations; the Separation of Insureds condition expressly carves it out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Services performed by its salaried staff and any employees' is broad but plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-back gives the Insurer 'sole discretion', which sits awkwardly against IX.M requiring consent not to be unreasonably withheld.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line, absolute: any claim by any insured against any other insured, with no carve-outs at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'insured' sweeps in employees and additional insureds, the exclusion arguably swallows the Separation of Insureds condition and the additional-insured grant in Endorsement 2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Intentional disregard of, or knowing, willful, or deliberate non-compliance with, any law ... or instruction of any governmental agency' is a broad and fact-laden standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope depends on 'responsible person', and it is expressly carved out of the Separation of Insureds condition; consistent overall.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In existence and reported to a responsible person' plus the tail 'including any pollution conditions discovered during the normal course of further investigation' is dense, and the carve-out list is misnumbered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-outs depend on a Schedule of Known Conditions Endorsement that is not attached, and the exclusion overlaps Coverage B, which is designed to insure pre-existing conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, with a clear soil-and-groundwater carve-back; a missing opening quotation mark is immaterial.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the asbestos exclusion; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Materially increases the likelihood or severity' of a pollution condition compared with 'intended uses or operations identified' in the application is an open-textured standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It measures change against application materials, tying it to IX.F Representations and the Fraud exclusion; complementary rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Naturally occurring materials' is undefined and vague, and the carve-back switches to 'naturally occurring substances ... as a result of human activities or human processes' — a wording shift that changes the boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether a biological agent present on a farm is a 'naturally occurring material' interacts directly with the Endorsement 12 definition of 'pollution condition'; a genuine but unnamed interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward site-based exclusion with a schedule-based carve-back.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8.III deletes and replaces this exclusion entirely, and its carve-back points to a Schedule of Non-Owned Disposal Sites Endorsement that is not attached.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'and' joining the knowledge requirement to alternatives '1. or 2.' makes the structure slightly hard to parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both limbs reference schedules ('if any') that do not exist in this policy, so the exclusion operates without its intended qualifications.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Automobile, aircraft, watercraft, railcar or other conveyance' is a list with an unbounded catch-all, and 'loading or unloading' is a classic point of dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10.III deletes and replaces this exclusion, and its carve-back references 'contingent transportation', whose definition Endorsement 10.II removed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Attributable, whether directly or indirectly ... regardless of any other cause' is broad but a standard anti-concurrent-causation formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the wide 'war' definition, which itself reaches government confiscation or destruction of property; that breadth is the only friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As soon as practicable' is the perennially litigated notice standard, and 'Notice should include' is permissive where the rest is mandatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the claims-made requirement of written report 'during the policy period' in I.A/I.B, so two different notice standards apply to the same event.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated duty list, though the numbering has dropped items 3 and 4; 'reasonably require' is a familiar standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforced by IX.C.2, which conditions suit on full compliance with policy terms; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Absolute consent requirement with a single emergency carve-out; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4.V deletes and replaces this subsection (dropping 'express'), so two versions of the consent standard are printed in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Make every attempt to mitigate' and 'in the sole judgment of the Insurer' are both loose, and the sentence is broken by stray spacing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Sole judgment' is hard to square with IX.M, which requires the Insurer's consent not to be unreasonably withheld, and with VII.C's consent requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grants the extended reporting period 'following Cancellation ... or nonrenewal', saying nothing about ordinary expiry of the three-year term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsections C and D (as replaced by Endorsement 7) condition the periods only on there being no replacement insurance, which implies a broader trigger than A recites.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deeming rule is precise and the limitations are stated flatly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the definition of 'extended reporting period' and with the claims-made notices; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sixty days, no charge, conditioned on not buying replacement insurance; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 7 deletes and replaces this subsection with a ninety-day period, so the printed sixty-day text is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not more than two hundred percent of the full premium' and the request deadline are precise, if one-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 7 replaces it with a thirty-three month version, leaving two different durations in the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence of paragraph 2 — 'The effective date and hour of cancellation stated in the notice shall be the end of the policy period' — is an odd deeming, and the carve-out sentence about affiliates reads backwards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 9 deletes and replaces paragraph 2 with a ninety-day version, and paragraph 3's pro rata refund is hard to reconcile with the 100% minimum-earned premium in Item 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent of the insured's ability to provide such access' and 'reasonable notice' are soft but ordinary; the disclaimer is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Audit rights run three years after termination while the extended reporting period may run longer; a small mismatch only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unless all of the Policy terms have been fully complied with' is an absolute condition precedent to suit whose reach is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on access to the courts alongside the Jurisdiction and Venue condition and the Service of Suit Endorsement, which promise submission to a competent court.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence about not dropping down 'in the event of the insolvency ... of any underlying insurer' presupposes underlying insurance this policy does not have.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy is written primary over a self-insured retention, so the excess/drop-down language has no counterpart elsewhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waterfall is stated in a definite order, though 'the limit of coverage' is an undefined phrasing next to 'Limits of Liability'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the retention scheme in Section II; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Converts application statements into warranties in three flat sentences; harsh but unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with the Fraud exclusion and cancellation for misrepresentation; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out list cites 'Cancellation condition 2.a.' — non-payment of premium — where the fraud provision 2.b is plainly what is meant, a cross-reference error that changes the clause's effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies severability only to 'named insureds' while the exclusions it carves out speak of 'insured', leaving additional insureds and employees unaddressed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard excess-and-non-contribution wording with a clear exception for policies written excess of this one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits with IX.D's excess language and with the multiple-policy-period rule in II.H; broadly consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Exclusive jurisdiction of the State of New York' does not say whether it means the courts of New York or any court sitting in New York, is expressed as a submission rather than a venue mandate, and is immediately qualified by a removal savings sentence pointing to federal court.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A comprehensive choice-of-law sentence naming one state; definite on its face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as provided by endorsement and attached to this Policy' is garbled but its sense is recoverable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence headings disclaimer; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It undercuts reliance on captions such as 'Jurisdiction and Venue', which matters given that clause's dispute, but does not contradict anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not be unreasonably withheld, delayed, conditioned, or denied' is a familiar and workable standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare schedule adding one named insured; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits V.S and the Separation of Insureds condition; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Solely with respect to their vicarious liability arising out of any named insured's direct liability' is a narrow and somewhat circular grant, and the sentence ends without a full stop.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grant, sublimit and deductible period are all stated numerically; 'directly attributable' is the only soft term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net profit or loss ... that would have been realized' is inherently counterfactual, and limb 2's payroll exclusions are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with 'business interruption' and the appraisal mechanism; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary partial or complete suspension' leaves the threshold of a partial suspension undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 'period of interruption' and IV.B, the endorsement supplies start and end rules; broadly coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-item pointer definition; the missing closing quote on 'Extra expense' is trivial.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Confined to a 'covered location under development' and then lists five specific expense heads with no catch-all; numbering is corrupted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It states only when the period begins and never says when it ends, an incomplete definition on its face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line, tied to 'suspension' of a rented covered location; 'fost' is an obvious scanning error for 'lost'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the 'suspension' and 'business income' definitions; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Untenantable for the purposes identified to the Insurer at the inception of the Policy' points outside the document to unspecified communications.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A counterfactual start date for delayed operations, stated in one clear sentence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Remedied to the point at which normal operations could reasonably be restored' and the exclusion of losses from 'unfavorable business conditions caused by the impact of the covered pollution condition' are both open to competing readings.
